worked.problem: Classify 6 in its smallest set and list every larger set.
actions: Point to 6 as a positive counting number
illuminate W, Z, Q and R outward. Written: 6 ∈ N
worked.misconception: Check 6 = 6/1. Error: calling Q its *smallest* set.
worked.memo: Point to 6 as a positive counting number; place the 6 token in N; illuminate W, Z, Q and R outward. Written: 6 ∈ N; therefore 6 ∈ W, Z, Q, R.

worked.problem: Is 0 natural or whole under the displayed convention? List its memberships.
actions: place 0 in W but outside N
illuminate Z, Q, R. Written: 0 ∈ W, Z, Q, R
worked.misconception: Check 0 = 0/1. Error: silently changing the N convention.
worked.memo: Display N beginning at 1; show 0 at the origin; place 0 in W but outside N; illuminate Z, Q, R. Written: 0 ∈ W, Z, Q, R; 0 ∉ N.

actions: note it is an integer, not whole
illuminate Q and R. Written: −7 ∈ Z, Q, R
worked.misconception: Check −7 = −7/1. Error: assuming a negative number cannot be rational.
worked.memo: Place −7 left of zero; note it is an integer, not whole; move token into Z; illuminate Q and R. Written: −7 ∈ Z, Q, R; −7 ∉ W.

worked.problem: Classify 3/4 and justify whether it is an integer.
actions: Draw four equal parts with three filled
worked.misconception: Check 0 < 3/4 < 1. Error: calling every fraction an integer.
worked.memo: Draw four equal parts with three filled; write numerator and nonzero denominator; place in Q outside Z; illuminate R. Written: 3/4 ∈ Q, R; 3/4 ∉ Z.

worked.misconception: Check −5 ÷ 2 = −2.5. Error: treating negative decimals as irrational.
worked.memo: Mark −2.5 on a line; rewrite −2.5 = −25/10 = −5/2; place in Q; illuminate R.

actions: write x = 0.333…, 10x = 3.333…, subtract to get 9x = 3, hence x = 1/3
worked.misconception: Check 1/3 = 0.333…. Error: equating nonterminating with irrational.
worked.memo: Highlight repeating digit; write x = 0.333…, 10x = 3.333…, subtract to get 9x = 3, hence x = 1/3; move into Q; illuminate R.

actions: replace √49 with 7 as the principal root
place in N, illuminate W, Z, Q, R.
worked.misconception: Check 7² = 49 and √49 ≥ 0. Error: classifying by the radical sign or using ±7 as √49.
worked.memo: Highlight radical; pair 7 × 7 = 49; replace √49 with 7 as the principal root; place in N, illuminate W, Z, Q, R.

actions: Show √4 = 2 as a contrast, then locate √2 between 1 and 2
state its decimal does not terminate or repeat
place √2 in I, illuminate R only.
Check: Check 1² < 2 < 2²; do not claim a finite decimal is exact.
worked.misconception: Check 1² < 2 < 2²; do not claim a finite decimal is exact. Error: all radicals are irrational.
worked.memo: Show √4 = 2 as a contrast, then locate √2 between 1 and 2; state its decimal does not terminate or repeat; place √2 in I, illuminate R only.
worked.check: Check: Check 1² < 2 < 2²; do not claim a finite decimal is exact.

actions: apply the outside negative sign to obtain −9
place in Z, illuminate Q and R.
worked.misconception: Check −√81 = −9, not +9; 9² = 81. Error: dropping the outside minus.
worked.memo: Find principal √81 = 9; apply the outside negative sign to obtain −9; place in Z, illuminate Q and R.

worked.problem: Classify π and decide whether 22/7 is the same number.
actions: draw an approximation arrow from 22/7 to π without an equality sign
Check: Check 22/7 ≈ π but is not equal.
worked.misconception: Check 22/7 ≈ π but is not equal. Error: an approximation inherits the exact number's set.
worked.memo: Put π in I; draw an approximation arrow from 22/7 to π without an equality sign; show 22/7 is in Q; illuminate R for both.
worked.check: Check: Check 22/7 ≈ π but is not equal.

worked.misconception: Substitute back: −√16/2 = −4/2 = −2. Error: applying minus to denominator or classifying before simplification.
worked.memo: Evaluate √16 = 4; retain outside minus: −4/2; divide to get −2; place in Z; illuminate Q and R.

worked.problem: A learner says 2/0 is irrational because it is not rational. Diagnose the first error.
actions: show division by zero is undefined
distinguish not rational from irrational real.
Check: Check no real y satisfies 0 × y = 2.
worked.misconception: Check no real y satisfies 0 × y = 2. Error: taking complement of Q in all expressions instead of within R.
worked.memo: Highlight denominator 0; show division by zero is undefined; block the token outside R; distinguish not rational from irrational real.
worked.check: Check: Check no real y satisfies 0 × y = 2.

worked.problem: Classify 0.101001000100001…, where each successive 1 has one more zero before it.
actions: note the decimal never terminates and has no repeating fixed block
Check: Check the displayed rule continues indefinitely.
worked.misconception: Check the displayed rule continues indefinitely. Error: mistaking visible repeated 1s for a repeating decimal period.
worked.memo: Mark successive increasing zero runs; note the decimal never terminates and has no repeating fixed block; place in I, illuminate R.
worked.check: Check: Check the displayed rule continues indefinitely.

actions: move token from an unclassified radical expression into N
worked.misconception: Check √50 = 5√2, so ratio is 5. Error: declaring the original expression irrational because each radical looks irrational.
worked.memo: Confirm denominator is nonzero; combine radicals for positive values: √(50/2) = √25; evaluate 5; move token from an unclassified radical expression into N; illuminate W, Z, Q, R.

worked.problem: Classify √(−9) in the real-number system and explain why it differs from −√9.
actions: Show the negative lies *inside* the radical
no real square is −9, so place outside R
contrast with −√9 = −3, which belongs to Z, Q, R.
Check: Check every real square is ≥0.
worked.misconception: Check every real square is ≥0. Error: moving the minus outside the radical.
worked.memo: Show the negative lies *inside* the radical; no real square is −9, so place outside R; contrast with −√9 = −3, which belongs to Z, Q, R.
worked.check: Check: Check every real square is ≥0.

A. Principal root 8; B classifies by appearance, C/D are broader.

practice.memo: D. Finite 3.14 = 314/100; A/C conflate approximation, B replaces ≈ with =.
A. 0/6 = 0; B broader, C ignores valid fraction, D starts N at 1.

practice.memo: C. No division by zero; A/D falsely assign a value, B treats every non-rational expression as irrational.
B. √9 = 3; A classifies before simplification, C/D broader.

A. B omits irrationals; C omits negatives; D ignores a/1.
